title: Gate Design and Stage-Dependent Incentives in Retail Proprietary-Trading Evaluations: Why Passing Is Not Standalone Evidence of Skill, and Why the Product Fails to Pay Under Measured Trading Constraints
abstract: arXiv:2609.14859v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Retail proprietary-trading firms sell a two-stage product: a paid evaluation that must reach a profit target before breaching a trailing drawdown, then a funded account that must survive a minimum window and a consistency rule before a payout. We show the geometry of this contract creates incentives that differ by stage and make passing a poor standalone signal of skill. Under end-of-day trailing the evaluation rewards a fast, lumpy cadence while the funded account punishes it, by a factor of nine in the joint gate. The evaluation is defeatable at zero skill: position sizing alone yields a pass probability near 0.40, against a measured cohort rate of 0.168. Pass probability rises with skill, but a real edge and aggressive sizing move it by nearly the same amount, so a pass rate confounds the two. translated_title: 零售自营交易评估中的门槛设计与阶段依赖性激励：为什么通过评估并非技能的独立证据，以及为什么在实测交易约束下该产品无法实现支付
translated_abstract: 零售自营交易公司销售一种两阶段产品：首先是付费评估阶段，要求在突破追踪回撤（trailing drawdown）之前达到利润目标；随后是资金账户阶段，必须在获得支付前通过最短时间窗口和一致性规则。我们展示了这种合约的几何结构会产生因阶段而异的激励，并使“通过评估”成为衡量技能的糟糕独立信号。在日终追踪回撤机制下，评估阶段奖励快速、块状的交易节奏，而资金账户阶段则惩罚这种节奏，在联合门槛下惩罚幅度高达九倍。评估可以在零技能条件下被攻克：仅凭仓位管理即可获得接近0.40的通过概率，而实测群体通过率仅为0.168。通过概率确实随技能提升而上升，但真实的交易优势与激进的仓位管理对通过概率的影响几乎相同，因此通过率无法区分二者。在简化的合约模型下，卖方的利润空间受限于感知门槛概率与实际门槛概率之间的差距……
tldr: 该论文通过建模揭示，零售自营交易公司的两阶段评估产品存在阶段依赖的激励错配——零技能下仅凭仓位管理即可达到约0.40的通过概率，且通过率无法区分真实交易优势与激进仓位操作，因此“通过评估”不是技能的独立证据，该产品在实测交易约束下难以实现支付。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates that the two-stage evaluation product of retail proprietary-trading firms creates stage-dependent incentive misalignment—passing can be achieved at zero skill through position sizing alone (~0.40 pass probability versus a measured cohort rate of 0.168), and pass rates confound real trading edges with aggressive sizing, making passing poor standalone evidence of skill and the product fail to pay under measured trading constraints.
